### About the event

You can spend four days collecting conference contacts - or 45 minutes actually getting to know a few security people.

A free 45-minute waterfront walk. No stage, no microphone, no forced networking. Come on your own - it's normal here.

### Who is this for?

Auditors, bug hunters, smart-contract security researchers, protocol engineers, and security-curious Devcon ticket holders. Everyone is welcome regardless of gender or experience.

### Why come?

Find fellow researchers, compare real lessons from hacks and audits, and start conversations that aren't another panel Q&A.

Conversation starter (optional): What's one security red flag you wish every DeFi user understood?

### Meet-up details

Date: Sunday, 1 November 2026

Walk: 7:00-7:45 AM IST. Arrive by 6:50 AM so you can find the group before we start.

Pace: Easy walking for 45 minutes; a gentle jog is optional. No fitness requirements.

Bring: Drinking water, comfortable shoes, a charged phone and curiosity.

- Mapped meeting landmark: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Monument, 1 Juhu Tara Road, Juhu, Mumbai 400049. Use the map pin on this event page, not the conference venue.
- Exact entrance and route: The host will confirm the precise side of the landmark and safe public pedestrian path in a Luma update before the event. This is a proposed meeting area, not an inspected route yet.

### Tickets and joining

This walk is FREE and registration is open without a fixed attendance cap. A valid Devcon 8 ticket is required to participate. The RSVP does not provide a Devcon ticket. Confirm that you hold one in the sign-up form; never upload your QR code or wallet secrets.

Please be considerate: Respect pedestrians, other attendees and different paces; no unsolicited pitches. We'll stay in public pedestrian areas and avoid traffic lanes and unsafe shoreline sections. If weather, access or route checks require a change, registered guests will receive updated joining details in Luma.

Hosted independently by Veerendra Vamshi (Proof of Audits). Not an official Devcon or Ethereum Foundation event.

## DeFi Security Summit 2026

- Record: `ibw-official-defi-security-summit-day-1-11-01`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-01T04:30:00.000Z

### About the event

The fifth DeFi Security Summit takes place at Courtyard by Marriott Mumbai International Airport on November 1 and 2, 2026, from 10:00 to 18:00 IST each day. It is intended for security researchers, auditors, protocol builders and the wider DeFi community. The venue address is CTS 215, Andheri-Kurla Road, opposite Carnival Cinemas, Andheri East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400093.

The organizer has published a [2026 talk directory](https://defisecuritysummit.org/2026/agenda), although its Luma description still says speakers and program details are forthcoming. The directory identifies the following talks with the November 1 and 2 Marriott summit. Individual session times and rooms remain to be assigned.

### Published talks

Hudson Jameson, head of Web3 at CertiK, revisits the 2017 Parity multisig hacks.

Steffen Kux, co-founder and co-CEO of corpus.core, discusses trustless transaction analysis before Ethereum wallet signatures.

Dmytro Matviiv, CEO of HackenProof, examines changes in crowdsourced security, including Code4rena and Hats Finance.

Natalia Klaus, verification engineer at Runtime Verification, covers a pipeline from production Rust to Lean 4 proofs using AI provers.

Kirk Baird, executive director of Sigma Prime, examines single points of failure in blockchain security.

Shebin John, senior research engineer at Safe Research, presents a deny-by-default policy engine for Safe.

Rahul Saxena, founder of Bluethroat Labs, addresses attestation gaps in private AI and TEE-backed DeFi.

Paul Clemson, audit engineer at Quantstamp, examines collateral flows when auditing Polymarket V2.

Kalp Shah, smart contract auditor at QuillAudits, discusses circuit-level exploits in DeFi.

Jacob Czepluch covers Core Solidity.

Michael Lewellen, head of solutions engineering at Turnkey, examines recovery mechanisms as an attack surface.

Don Josey, founder of Glossifi, asks how financial incentives affect security judgment.

Ofir Eliasi, CTO of Lava Foundation, covers security during live Cosmos-to-EVM migrations and the risks of unaudited RPC infrastructure.

Lokesh Joshi, blockchain and AI engineer, discusses autonomous defense for DeFi.

Mohamad Mansouri, Web3 security researcher at Dedaub, evaluates AI auditing against real smart-contract audits.

Victor Okafor, security researcher at QuillAudits, considers quantum threats beyond post-quantum signatures.

George Loukovitis, senior engineer at Dedaub, combines deterministic analysis and language models to detect unsafe ERC-20 behavior.

Akand Sitra of Hypernative covers real-time Web3 security monitoring.

Gerard Persoon, security researcher at Cantina, examines conversion between EVM bytecode and Solidity.

Anu Adeleke of QuillAudits presents a session on vulnerable Daml code.

Nemveer, senior security researcher at Certora, discusses ecosystem-specific security lessons from auditing NEAR.

Raj Kumar, security researcher at Certora, and senior threat researcher Sabanaku77 examine monitoring internals, chain data and incident response.

Henri Binsztok, co-founder and CEO of OKcontract Labs, examines how a multisig can approve an unintended transaction.

Uri Kirstein, product manager for Fordefi's blockchain team, discusses information missing from Safe transaction decoders.

Igor Gulamov, co-founder of SavantChat, applies AI auditing to consensus, mempools and peer-to-peer systems.

Viraz Malhotra, senior blockchain engineer and security researcher, introduces a methodology for AI-assisted auditing.

Nicolas Garcia, security researcher at OpenZeppelin, discusses when to deploy an AI auditor and disclose its findings.

Jochen Hoenicke, formal verification researcher at Certora, examines a self-liquidation issue in Morpho Midnight involving a callback window.

Josselin Feist, security researcher at Aave Labs, addresses security leadership.

Jeff Fei, security researcher at Ant International, presents SOAC and zero-trust smart-contract permission governance.

Jork Leonhardt, co-founder of Corpus Core GmbH, covers RPC trust failures affecting builders and monitoring tools.

Daniel Monzón, offensive security engineer at Halborn, discusses Web3 red-teaming methods.

Robert Reith, CEO and co-founder of Accretion and hackhack, examines bugs missed by AI tools.

Abhimanyu Nag, engineering manager at Muchlearning/Canvas, models cryptoeconomic attacks and adversaries in DeFi.

Andy M. Lee, founder and CEO of Mamori, examines what fuzzing establishes about smart-contract security.

Magnus Woodgate, lead security engineer at Asymmetric Research, has two listed talks on post-quantum signatures, stateful risks and Ethereum account security.

Joaquin Pereyra, lead security engineer at Coinspect, examines the discovery of and response to the Ill Bloom wallet-generation flaw.

Sumanjeet, maintainer of py-libp2p and unified-testing, shares security and operational lessons from py-libp2p and Py-IPFS-lite.

Julia Hardy, co-founder and head of investigations at zeroShadow, discusses using money-laundering intelligence to contain active exploits.

Davit Kobakhidze of Consensys Diligence discusses AI security challenges looking ahead to 2027.

Christian Vari, head of audit operations at Oak Security, presents an adversarial methodology for AI audits and a four-year study comparing audit findings with exploits.

Bernardo Codesido, head of security at RootstockLabs, discusses building a lasting crypto security team.

Nikita Belenkov, security engineer at Anza, examines running an audit competition.

Doris Benda, blockchain security engineer and auditor at ChainSecurity, covers dirty bits in Solidity.

Hrishikesh Bhat of Cantina examines the development of crowdsourced security beyond bounties.

Sofia Bobadilla, PhD student at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, discusses smart-contract invariants as a defense against attacks.

Zakaryae Boudi, founder of Tokenfrastructure Group, examines vulnerabilities created by the interaction of otherwise correct contracts.

Petar Calic, protocol lead at Spectra, covers the opportunities and pitfalls of formal verification with AI.

Lilian Cariou, security and formal-verification researcher at Certora, examines Aave V4's hub-and-spoke architecture.

Ivan Djordjevic, head of security and data protection at Degensoft, discusses the SOC 2 Type 2 observation period in a DeFi organization.

Matthias Egli, founding and managing partner of ChainSecurity, reviews hacks since Devcon 7.

John Ennis of Safe R&D examines onchain security markets in the context of offensive AI.

Elliot Friedman of Solidity Labs covers multisig backdoor detection and laptop security in governance-proposal workflows.

Josef Gattermayer, co-founder of ack3, compares frontier models for EVM auditing and examines practical fuzzing with coding agents.

Jelle (0xFlint) Goethals, founder of Flint Security, covers x402 integration requirements and indirect dependencies in DeFi trust relationships.

Neville Grech, co-founder of Dedaub, discusses symbolic execution for math-heavy code alongside AI tools.

Manu Sheel Gupta, technical lead and maintainer for libp2p, IPLD and Multiformats, examines a Gossipsub crash and its implications for AI security and DeFi infrastructure.

Peter Kacherginsky, security researcher and author of BlockThreat, surveys DeFi security in 2026.

George Kobakhidze of Consensys Diligence presents Certiflai and certification workflows.

Dima Kogan, CTO and co-founder of Fordefi, and Yaron Salman, its cryptography specialist, discuss MPC wallets and post-quantum readiness.

Kevin Lotz covers formal verification of stake pools and a practical application.

Yash Saraswat, smart contract engineer at ether.fi, presents a runtime security framework for liquid staking tokens.

Dhairya Sethi of Aave Labs' core smart-contract team and security researcher Tomer Ganor examine rounding and accounting risks in lending protocols.

Suryansh Singh, lead blockchain security researcher at OpenZeppelin, discusses security standards and weaknesses in evaluating Web3 AI security tools.

Anish Agrawal of Olympix draws lessons about real exploits from mutation testing.

Prabal Banerjee, co-founder of Avail, discusses responses to onchain surveillance infrastructure.

Yannis Smaragdakis, co-founder of Dedaub, covers reconstructing unverified contracts from bytecode and modeling fund flows using large linear-algebra systems.

Aarnav Bos, security engineer at Asymmetric Research, examines exploration and testing of consensus-protocol state spaces.

Sergey Khomutinin, senior Solidity engineer at Lido, discusses continuous auditing with language models.

nisedo, security engineer at Trail of Bits, presents lessons from AI bug hunting and a short session on evidence, questions and coverage in AI-assisted audits.

Rudra Singh of CertiK addresses frontend security audits.

Yuri Tkachenko, head of DeFi engineering at Lido, examines audit work after publication.

Jason W, security researcher, discusses real-time DeFi threat detection with stream engines.

Benjamin Flores, co-founder of Verity, covers formal verification in the context of AI.

Griff Green discusses collective approaches to DeFi security and costs.

Jan Kalivoda, co-founder of ack3.ai, addresses laptop security and components that audits leave outside their scope.

Jonathan Mevs, senior audit engineer at Quantstamp, examines agent-assisted formal verification.

Thomas Marques compares a simple LLM pipeline with more complex agent-based approaches.

Eugene Mamin, chief technical master at Lido Labs, presents the Lido and Nethermind Evergreen approach to continuous AI-assisted security.

- 0xa5df, senior security researcher at Certora, approaches auditing as system risk management.
- Christopher von Hessert, head of security at Polygon Labs, presents "Never Send a Human to Do a Machine's Job."
- Clément Moller, smart contract engineer at Origin Protocol, covers DeFi liveness testing with stateful invariants and replacing a staking oracle with beacon-chain proofs.

### Tickets and the Devcon continuation

Standard admission costs US$50 for both Marriott summit days. Students can use DSSSTUDENT at checkout for US$10 admission. Registration is through the summit's [Luma page](https://luma.com/9qtxqqxx).

DSS continues on November 3 as a community-led session at Devcon. Devcon admission is separate from the November 1 and 2 summit ticket. The organizer's agenda allows attendees to save a shortlist of talks; saving a talk does not reserve a seat.

## The Institutional Table: Private Dinner on Tokenization, Stablecoins and Security \| Mumbai

- Record: `ibw-official-the-institutional-table-private-dinner-on-tokenization-stablecoins-and-s-11-02`

### About the event

QuillAudits hosts The Institutional Table in Mumbai on November 2, 2026, from 19:30 to 22:30 IST, after the IBW conference and before Devcon opens. The invitation-only dinner is planned for 41 guests, with a short QuillAudits introduction followed by moderated discussion.

The intended participants include heads of digital assets, treasury and product at banks and asset managers; founders and senior executives of tokenization platforms and stablecoin issuers; exchanges; and fund partners with real-world-asset or stablecoin exposure. Regulators and policy leads participate by invitation

Discussion topics

- Moving funds, bonds and real-estate structures onchain, including ERC-3643, ERC-4626 vaults, NAV oracles, transfer restrictions and compliance controls.
- Stablecoins as payment infrastructure, including reserve attestations, mint and burn controls, blacklisting, freezing and issuer exploits.
- Security evidence that boards, regulators and counterparties can request before deploying capital: audits, formal verification, monitoring, key management and incident response.
- A closed-door review of institutional security incidents in 2026 and the warning signs or controls that could have identified problems earlier.

The dinner follows the Chatham House Rule and excludes recording, press and slide presentations. Participants may use information from the discussion without identifying its source.

Luma lists free registration, but registering is only a request for a seat. QuillAudits confirms guests personally and sends the exact BKC venue to those confirmed. The event is a seated, moderated dinner rather than a public panel or pitch session.

### About the event

CrossBar presents Open Silicon: IRIS Demo and Dabao Board Pickup at Devcon 8 in Mumbai on Thursday, November 5, 2026, from 11:00 to 16:00 IST. The open hardware clinic demonstrates non-destructive silicon inspection and open-source chip architectures.

### What to expect

The five-hour interactive clinic provides a hands-on look at open-source silicon manufacturing and validation:

Direct Q&A with chip design engineers and hardware security auditors on creating trustless cryptographic silicon.

- Live demonstrations of Infra-Red In-Situ (IRIS) inspection of the Daric silicon chip, verifying internal chip layout and proving the absence of hardware trojans.
- Hardware distribution desk where pre-registered developers pick up their Dabao RISC-V open evaluation boards.
- Technical teardowns explaining how physical unclonable functions (PUFs) and secure enclaves are manufactured on open-source instruction sets.

### Who should attend

### Venue and schedule

## Glamsterdam Readiness Clinic: 1:1s with ChainSecurity Engineers @ Devcon

- Record: `ibw-c9nw11qi`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-03T04:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/c9nw11qi>

### About the event

Glamsterdam changes how gas is accounted for, and some contracts will behave differently without a single line of code changing.

Our research found that the upcoming Glamsterdam hard fork affects how many smart contracts handle failed calls. We so far identified 13 real-world examples affected by this change.

All week at Devcon, ChainSecurity engineers are running private 1:1 sessions. Bring your call paths and we'll help you work out whether Glamsterdam affects your protocol, or discuss potential solutions.

Contracts that warrant particular review are those that continue after a failed subcall, for example to record a permanent failure, process batches or switch to a fallback, as well as proxies and intermediaries. Protocol teams should:recalculate the gas their failure paths need under both Osaka and Glamsterdam rulescheck for storage slots that are set and cleared within the same transactionrevalidate fixed gas budgets and thresholds against the proposed costs and gas-accounting rulestest direct and nested subcall failures, including out-of-gas failures across different gas budgets and reservoir balances, and verify that insufficient gas cannot permanently disable retries or invalidate otherwise valid claimsBefore booking, please read the blog to see whether this applies to you:

Glamsterdam Hard Fork: When Spent Gas Comes BackAfter you RSVP here, our team will ping you to schedule your 1:1 and tell you what to share beforehand, so we can come prepared.

Starknet operates as a validity rollup on Ethereum, which provides settlement. Its purpose is to enable a true peer-to-peer economy.

### About MetaMask

https://metamask.io/?utm_source=luma

MetaMask is the world's leading self-custody web3 platform with 19 million monthly active users. Developed by Consensys, MetaMask is the most beloved and trusted way a global user base relies on to mint and collect NFTs, join DAOs, play games and participate in DeFi protocols.

### About Monad Foundation

Monad Foundation supports the growth and decentralization of the Monad ecosystem, a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain designed for speed, scalability, and low transaction costs. The Foundation empowers developers, builders, and communities to create the next generation of decentralized applications, from DeFi and trading to emerging onchain use cases.

### About ARKIV

ARKIV is building decentralized data infrastructure designed to make data programmable, accessible, and verifiable. By enabling developers to build applications that interact with decentralized data, ARKIV supports new possibilities for AI agents, autonomous applications, and the next generation of onchain services.

### About ENS

Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is the decentralized naming protocol for Ethereum, making web3 more accessible through human-readable names. ENS enables users, developers, and applications to replace complex blockchain addresses with simple identities, while providing essential infrastructure for decentralized identity, payments, and interactions between humans and AI agents.

### About STRATO

STRATO is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain platform designed to help enterprises build and deploy real-world blockchain applications. By combining blockchain infrastructure with enterprise-grade capabilities, STRATO enables organizations to develop secure, scalable solutions for tokenization, digital assets, and decentralized business processes.

### About Consensys Diligence

Consensys Diligence is a leading blockchain security team specializing in smart contract audits, security assessments, and developer security tooling. With extensive experience securing Ethereum-based protocols and decentralized applications, Diligence helps developers identify vulnerabilities, strengthen smart contract security, and build safer onchain experiences.

## Whitepaper Reading Club: Multiple Concurrent Proposers + Rise of PropAMMs

- Record: `ibw-wprc-kol-261104-at-monad-blitz-devcon`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-04T09:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/wprc-kol-261104-at-monad-blitz-devcon>

### About the event

Multiple Concurrent Proposers + The Rise of PropAMMs1. Cadence Extreme PipeliningCadence redesigns BFT block production by replacing a single leader with multiple proposers running in parallel. Each slot reaches consensus independently, so it does not wait for earlier blocks or network delays. It is built on two parts: Chorus, a fast 3-round consensus protocol, and Conductor, which controls when new slots open. Cadence provides short-term censorship resistance, hides proposals until they are revealed, and keeps the same security (3f+1 validators) and low latency as single-leader systems.

In simulations on Monad's 200-validator network with 5 proposers per slot, it achieved 219 ms average finality ( 167 ms speculative) and 50 ms average transaction wait time with 100 ms block intervals.

This is part of Monad Blitz: https://luma.com/Blitz-Mumbai-Devcon-20262. How Market Makers Are Reshaping Cross-Chain LiquidityTraditional AMMs, such as Uniswap, allow anyone to provide liquidity and earn trading fees. However, their prices typically update only when trades occur, leaving liquidity providers exposed to arbitrageurs who profit from outdated prices.

A new model, proprietary automated market makers (propAMMs), is changing this. Unlike traditional AMMs, propAMMs actively update prices without waiting for trades, allowing them to respond faster to market movements. By 2026, propAMMs accounted for more than half of SOL/USDC trading volume on Solana. The paper: Active Liquidity On Chain: Evidence from PropAMMs Across Chains (September 2026), was written by Ozan Solmaz (ETH Zurich), Lioba Heimbach (Category Labs), Jason Milionis (Category Labs)Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.38056FormatShort introduction and context setting to start.

A short walkthrough of the paper and its key ideas.

Questions and discussion grounded in the original source.

Moderator-led discussion with no promotions. Session Guides:Rongxin Zhang is the founder of Whitepaper Reading Club (WPRC). Previously, he lead Product at Cobo Custody, CKB, and was part of the founding team of Retsly, acquired by Zillow in 2015. He worked on decentarlized file storage research at Cornell Tech in 2017. Monad Foundation Monad is an institutional-grade blockchain built to power an open, global economy, enabling efficient money movement, tokenization, capital markets, and other financial applications. Built by a team from Jump Crypto.

Thank you Elton, and the team for always hosting us!!

About Whitepaper Reading ClubWe are a community of founders, researchers, and builders across Singapore, Malaysia, San Francisco, Bangkok, New York, Lagos, Taipei, and Hong Kong. We meet in person every month to read, discuss, and pressure-test the latest blockchain papers, protocols, and technical ideas.

Learn more: Website - Summaries - CalendarWe create detailed, easy-to-understand summaries for each paper and have held 80+ sessions since June 2023, covering Account Abstraction, Parallel Chains, EIPs, the Bitcoin ecosystem, and AI x Crypto. We are ecosystem-agnostic, not for profit, and focused on projects with technical, product, or social innovation.

ArQ and Abhiraj Mengade host Diyas: NEAR @Devcon in Mumbai on November 4, 2026, from 16:00 to 20:00 IST. The Diwali-themed gathering uses a team game to demonstrate NEAR cross-chain intents, with participants playing the roles of chains, swaps and confidential transactions.

Before arrival, NEAR AI uses each attendee's RSVP answers to create a physical persona card with a custom animated face and fragments of an intent. Participants find five other people and combine their fragments into a valid cross-chain instruction. The organizer's example is a confidential swap from NEAR to Solana.

The completed instruction goes to an Executor Booth, where an operator executes a US$1 to US$2 onchain micro-intent, with a testnet fallback, and prints the transaction hash. The group receives a Polaroid with the hash and a trusted execution environment (TEE) attestation on the back. That proof can be exchanged at the desk for Diwali merchandise offered as a game reward rather than for sale.

Attendees should complete the RSVP questionnaire and bring a phone and wallet handle. Solo participants can form groups at the door.

Registration is free and requires host approval. The organizer describes a Mumbai workspace and rooftop setting; the public location listing identifies Mumbai without a specific street address.

### About the event

Frontier of Intelligence Hackathon brings developers, founders, researchers and designers working on AI, Web3 and autonomous systems to Mumbai from November 5, 2026, at 09:00 IST to November 6 at 17:00 IST.

Hosted by Lakshmi, it offers mentorship in AI, cryptography and protocol design, alongside infrastructure partners for compute, LLM tooling and Web3 development. The organizer also describes routes to accelerator, grant and venture-capital opportunities

Technical tracks Autonomous AI Agents and Multi-Agent Systems: This track covers agents that coordinate onchain, execute financial or governance actions, interact with smart contracts and collaborate with other agents. It emphasizes agent economies, agent-to-agent commerce and onchain execution layers. Decentralized AI Infrastructure: Projects can address decentralized compute markets, verifiable inference, zero-knowledge machine learning (ZK-ML), distributed training or model marketplaces. Intelligence for Real-World Systems: Applications include healthcare AI infrastructure, climate coordination, financial intelligence, defense and cyber coordination, and autonomous supply chains

Announced awards

The US$5,000 grand prize is for the most impactful project across the tracks, assessed on technical depth, originality, real-world potential and scalability. Track winners are offered US$3,000 each. ### About the event

IMPORTANT: Access to the hub is only for Devcon ticket holders. Get yours here. (https://devcon.org/en/tickets/)

Privacy gives you the freedom to act on your own terms.

Join us at the Practical Privacy Day to meet the builders working on privacy across Ethereum and beyond, and learn how you can take more control over your data.

You'll hear how teams are bringing privacy to Ethereum's L1 and explore different approaches to privacy-centric L2s. See open-source hardware wallets in action and learn how to prepare for a post-quantum future. We'll explore practical tools you can use day-to-day, from VPNs, AI tools that respect your data, to open-source alternatives.

The day is designed for anyone and everyone interested in on and offchain privacy solutions. No technical knowledge required.

## Clear-Signing & Wallet Security @ DEVCON

- Record: `ibw-luma-evt-7bLYYfCCvXDasQt`
- Source: [ibw-side-events.json](sources/ibw-side-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-07T06:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/kwi8jlpk>

### About the event

The ERC-8009 team is hosting an event dedicated to clear signing and ways to achieve it.

The existing and experimental solutions will be demonstrated using Ledger and Trezor devices.

Clear signing is a solution to Blind Signing, which is the single biggest security threat currently facing everyday Web3 users and protocol teams. It occurs when a hardware wallet cannot decode the transaction and present it in human language, so the end user approving the wallet transaction is left guessing whether the transaction is exactly what they intend to send. In many cases, unsuspecting users simply approve such transactions, accepting the risk.

Even though hardware wallets are commonly thought of as the ultimate security solution, they are still prone to attacks involving "blind signing". For example, that's exactly what happened to Bybit when the Safe code was modified and the hardware wallet couldn't provide a human-language explanation of the transaction (the famous $1.5B hack).

Join us during DEVCON Mumbai 2026 for a practical session exploring Clear-Signing solutions, amongst which ERC-8009 (Proxy Clear Signing) will be presented, with demos on real hardware devices.

### About the event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, an intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically a 1/16th-scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and a camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what the fastest way to do it is!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

Inflation, purchasing power, and the importance of sound money

What Bitcoin is and why it was created

Bitcoin's fixed supply and monetary properties

## RWA新階段：實物資產如何真正上鏈

- Record: `luma-crypto-gNTVHMUFj01ZOGH`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-02T06:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/vm8nxzx2>

### About the event

RWA 新階段:實物資產如何真正上鏈 宏觀週期之下,RWA 的價值重估與落地路徑

適逢 2026 香港金融科技週,國富量子聯合星路 Finloop,邀請來自金融機構、區塊鏈基礎設施與實物資產領域的嘉賓齊聚上環,用一個下午的時間,聊透 RWA 從「概念」走向「落地」的關鍵一步。

隨著香港 RWA 與穩定幣監管框架逐步完善,越來越多實物資產開始嘗試上鏈。但一項資產究竟如何完成確權、結構設計、代幣化發行,並最終進入二級市場流通?本場活動將以亞洲首個加拿大油氣資產通證化項目為案例,從宏觀環境、交易結構、鏈上技術到底層資產,完整拆解實物資產上鏈的全流程。

你將收穫

- 全球宏觀變局下,RWA 賽道的機會與風險判斷
- 一個真實能源資產 RWA 項目的完整結構拆解
- 資產代幣化背後的技術與鏈上基礎設施
- 與機構投資者、項目方及生態夥伴的深度交流

議程安排

Jacky Kong|Head of HK, Ava Labs

Daisy|COO,鑰坤科技

David Wang |Partner, Jun He Law Offices

- 嘉賓簽到
- 主題分享 01|宏觀經濟:全球擾動頻發下的宏觀前瞻。主講:李總,中金香港資產管理部副總經理
- 主題分享 02|RWA 案例:亞洲首個加拿大油氣資產通證化項目全解析。主講:Charles Zeng,國富量子 Global Head of Digital Assets
- 主題分享 03|上鏈技術:資產代幣化技術與鏈上基礎設施。主講:Colin,星路科技執行董事

### About the event

RWA 与稳定币支付正从概念探索走向业务落地。随着资产发行、交易分销、支付结算和托管服务逐渐交织，机构在拓展业务的同时，也需要面对合规要求、风控体系、跨境协作与安全应急等现实挑战。

为此，慢雾(SlowMist) 携手君合律师事务所，将于 11 月 2 日在香港举办「架构破局，风控筑底｜2026 香港 RWA 与稳定币支付机构闭门峰会」行业交流活动。

本次闭门峰会将邀请相关领域的机构代表，围绕 RWA 与稳定币支付的商业实践和风险治理展开交流，探讨业务如何落地、机构如何协作，以及如何为快速发展的市场筑牢安全与合规基础

活动信息

活动时间：2026 年 11 月 2 日（星期一）14:00-18:30

活动地点：香港中环友邦金融中心

活动主办：慢雾(SlowMist) 、君合律师事务

活动议程

即将发

主办方信息

慢雾科技 SlowMist

慢雾科技是一家专注区块链生态安全的威胁情报公司，成立于 2018 年 1 月，由一支拥有十多年一线网络安全攻防实战经验的团队创建，团队成员曾打造了拥有世界级影响力的安全工程。慢雾科技已是国际化的区块链安全头部公司，主要提供"由 AI 驱动、从威胁发现到威胁防御一体化、因地制宜"的安全解决方案，服务全球众多头部及知名的项目，已有商业客户上千家，客户分布在十几个主要国家与地区。

慢雾科技积极参与区块链安全行标、国标及国际标准的推进工作，是国内首批进入工信部《2018 年中国区块链产业白皮书》的单位，成立不到两年就获得「国家高新技术企业」认定。慢雾科技在「网络安全精英嘉许计划(CSPA)2025 」中，荣获香港警务处网络安全及科技罪案调查科颁发的"网络安全卓越贡献奖"；旗下反洗钱追踪分析平台 MistTrack ，亦在 HKICT Awards 2025 评选中荣获 FinTech (RegTech: Regulatory and Risk Management) 金奖。慢雾科技在新型加密货币犯罪调查方面有很多积累，研究成果被多个国际组织和政府部门引用，包括但不限于：联合国安理会、联合国毒品与犯罪问题办公室。

慢雾科技的安全解决方案包括：SlowMist AI、安全审计、威胁情报(BTI)、防御部署等服务并配套有加密货币反洗钱追踪分析平台(MistTrack)、面向大型机构的反洗钱合规引擎(SlowMist KYT)、假充值漏洞扫描、Web3 威胁情报与动态安全监测(MistEye)、被黑档案库(SlowMist Hacked) 等 SaaS 型安全产品。基于成熟有效的安全服务及安全产品，慢雾科技联动国际顶级的安全公司，如 Akamai、BitDefender、RC²、天际友盟、IPIP 等及海内外加密货币知名项目方、司法鉴定、执法机构等，从威胁发现到威胁防御上提供了一体化因地制宜的安全解决方案。慢雾科技在行业内曾独立发现并公布数多起通用高风险的区块链安全漏洞，得到业界的广泛关注与认可。给区块链生态带来安全感是慢雾科技努力的方向。

## Ethereum Classic Mumbai

- Record: `luma-crypto-TQDZinnxGDGJiHK`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-02T13:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/flt0wvtq>

### About the event

Ethereum and Ethereum Classic were once the same chain, until the DAO hard fork in 2016 sent them down separate paths. Ethereum later moved to Proof of Stake, while Classic stayed with Proof of Work. Ten years on, ETC enters its second decade, and every chain now faces new threats from quantum computers and AI.

We're a 15-minute walk from Ethereum Cypherpunk Congress #3 (https://congress.web3privacy.info/), and we invite you to this casual evening after it closes, the night before Devcon 8 opens, to pull up a chair and talk with Ethereum Classic developers and contributors.

### Who It's For

Builders on any EVM chain, node runners and miners, Congress and Devcon people, and anyone curious about Ethereum Classic.

Let's Talk About

We think ETC, the EVM chain with the greatest hash rate, is going to make a comeback.

Quantum computers threaten the elliptic-curve signatures every chain uses today, but ETC's consensus rests on hash-based Proof of Work, which shouldn't need to be migrated. Mining a block takes real hardware and energy, and there are no validator keys to steal or forge. Wallets are a different story, and we still need to figure out post-quantum signatures for ETC accounts, looking to Ethereum's research on this for inspiration.

Coming straight from the Cypherpunk Congress, we also thought it would be interesting to talk about the cypherpunk ideas ETC was built on, like censorship resistance and protocol neutrality, and about EVM symbiosis, since ETC and Ethereum share the EVM and the same contracts, tools and builders can work on both.

We think ETC is an underdog with a bright future, carried through ten years by people who stayed for principles that never die

:

- - 19:00 Doors open
- 19:30 A short welcome from Classix
- 19:45-22:00 Open discussions

### Venue

Leopold Cafe is a Classic Colaba Causeway landmark since 1871, with food, a full bar and a 15-minute walk from the Congress. Find us upstairs from 7pm.

Space at Leopold Cafe is limited and registrations are high. If we fill up, people in the ETC Mumbai Matrix room get priority, so join #etc-mumbai:matrix.org (https://matrix.to/#/#etc-mumbai:matrix.org) before the night.

Hosted by classix.dev (https://classix.dev)

論壇將透過四場主題演講及一場圓桌對談,聚焦美股投資機會、企業上市、券商與交易所的發展,以及證券 RWA 的合規與商業機遇。四場主題演講後,嘉賓將共同探討 AI 如何創造可投資的資產價值。

誠邀投資人、家族辦公室、金融與資產管理從業者、企業及資產方,以及 AI、Web3 與 RWA 領域的創業者參與,一同交流觀點、認識合作夥伴,探討產業發展與投資實踐。

### 論壇看點

1. 傳統金融 × RWA:探討傳統金融與資產代幣化的連接,以及金融機構的參與方式。 2. AI × 資產價值:討論 AI 如何改善資產的營運效率與價值,以及投資人如何評估相關機會。 3. 美股 × Web3 × 全球資本:從不同市場與投資視角出發,探討資產、機構及資本生態之間的合作。 4. 神秘嘉賓加持:兩位行業頂流大咖於晚間酒會亮相,開放自由交流,挖掘獨家合作機會。

## Can Regulated, Tokenized Assets Trade on Open Onchain Markets? Live Demo & Panel at Hong Kong Fintech Week

- Record: `luma-crypto-FLpxXn0aRE2igwO`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-03T08:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/tokenized-assets-open-markets-hong-kong>

### About the event

Can Regulated, Tokenized Assets Trade on Open Onchain Markets? is a closed-door session co-hosted by OpenZeppelin and Ethereum Institutional during Hong Kong Fintech Week, limited to 30 senior participants from banks, market infrastructure, and regulated asset issuers.

Bringing regulated assets onto open onchain markets raises real questions for institutions, from who enforces eligibility rules to how investor data stays protected, and there are good reasons most activity still runs on permissioned platforms.

This session explores what is technically possible today and where the open questions remain. Through a live walkthrough of a tokenized money market fund trading on an open onchain market, we'll look at how identity checks can run at every trade without personal data onchain, how a transfer agent can freeze an investor and have the market respect it on the next trade, and how a jurisdiction can be switched off while everyone else keeps trading.

A panel of industry experts then debates who should hold the keys when regulated assets meet open markets, and what it takes for institutions to go live. We close with a drinks reception.

Previous OpenZeppelin institutional events drew senior guests from firms including J.

P. Morgan, Citi, UBS, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, BNY, Fidelity, Mastercard, Deloitte, and more

:

- - Doors open and welcome coffee

16:30

- Live demo - Freeze, Block, Trade: A Regulated Fund on an Open Market (Bram Hoogenkamp, Product Manager, OpenZeppelin)

17:00

Panel: Who Holds the Keys? Control, Compliance and Open Markets (Panelists to be announced)

17:40

- Drinks reception and networkin

### About us

OpenZeppelin (https://www.openzeppelin.com/) is the security standard for onchain finance. Since 2015, its industry-standard smart contracts library has powered $37 trillion in value transferred, alongside 900+ security engagements for leading institutions, blockchain networks, and protocols including DTCC, Fidelity Digital Assets, WisdomTree, Aave, the Canton Foundation and the Ethereum Foundation. Learn more at openzeppelin.com (https://openzeppelin.com).

Ethereum Institutional (https://ethereuminstitutional.org/) is an independent non-profit accelerating institutional adoption of Ethereum, its L2s and the wider ecosystem. Founded in 2026 with anchor funding from BitMine, SharpLink, Joseph Lubin and Mihai Alisie, it helps institutions move from requirements to live onchain deployments. Learn more at ethereuminstitutional.org (https://ethereuminstitutional.org).

Event Photography

We'll be capturing photos and videos throughout the event. By attending, you agree that we may use event content (including your image) in our marketing materials, social media, and future promotions. If you prefer not to be photographed, please let us know at check-in.

Fireblocks 携手君合(JunHe)与 OneInfinity,诚邀支付服务提供商(PSP)、虚拟资产交易商(VA dealer)及虚拟资产交易平台(VATP)参加本场晚间交流活动。

稳定币产品正从试点走向规模化运营。上线之前,团队需要厘清三个问题:产品适用何种牌照,哪些管控措施经得起审计,一旦出现故障,损失由谁承担。三位嘉宾将分别围绕这三个问题展开分享。

演讲结合真实用例与技术细节,之后设交流环节,与业界同行、合作伙伴及开发者深入交流。

2026年11月3日 下午4:30 至 8:00 PM 香港时间

About Fireblocks: Fireblocks is the world's most trusted digital asset infrastructure company, empowering global institutions to build, manage and grow their business on the blockchain. With the industry's most scalable and secure platform, we streamline stablecoin payments, settlement, custody, tokenization, trading, accounting operations, and compliance reporting - enabling everything from institutional finance to consumer-facing digital experiences across the largest ecosystem of banks, payment providers, stablecoin issuers, exchanges and custodians.

Thousands of organizations - including Worldpay, BNY, Galaxy, and Revolut - trust Fireblocks to secure $16 trillion in digital asset transactions across 200+ blockchains. Learn more at fireblocks.com (https://www.fireblocks.com/).

About JunHe: Founded in Beijing in 1989, JunHe is one of China's leading law firms, with 15 offices worldwide and over 1,000 professionals.

Led by Jacqueline Qiao, Partner and Head of JunHe's Virtual Assets Practice, the team has extensive experience in virtual assets, digital finance and fintech, advising leading financial institutions, payment companies, virtual asset platforms and asset managers.

Our expertise spans virtual asset licensing, stablecoin issuance, RWA tokenization, digital asset trading and custody, and regulatory compliance. Combining expertise in financial regulation with an understanding of blockchain technology, we provide comprehensive legal support from transaction structuring and regulatory strategy to implementation and ongoing compliance.

About OneInfinity: OneInfinity insures the future of the digital economy. We design insurance for risks that traditional cover wasn't built for: digital asset custody, cyber, and management and professional liability for Web3, fintech and AI businesses.

Our team brings together underwriting and technical expertise, so we understand how wallets, keys and digital infrastructure fail, and we help clients reduce those risks as well as insure them. We serve exchanges, custodians, brokers and VA dealers, asset managers and any firm that handles digital assets across Hong Kong, the wider Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.

Alpha Ladder (https://www.alphaladder.com/): 專注打造賦能企業國際化及高淨值客戶的 Web2.5 全球數位金融生態。持有新加坡金管局(MAS)等多地金融牌照及許可(涵蓋跨境匯款,數位支付代幣,資本市場服務及貨幣服務業務等),依託法幣與穩定幣、傳統金融與數位資產的深度融合,為客戶打造高效、透明、無縫的跨境支付、財富管理、企業融資及財務顧問等一站式金融服務體系。

SPD (https://www.linkedin.com/company/south-pacific-digital-services/?originalSubdomain=hk): South Pacific Digital 是一家立足香港、面向全球市场的数字金融企业,专注于以稳定币技术推动全球支付创新与 AI 智能体商业发展。我们以SPD美元稳定币为核心产品,采用1:1美元锚定机制,并以可验证的储备资产提供支持。依托集团持有的瓦努阿图稳定币牌照及亚太地区的监管布局,我们将合规运营、储备透明与安全保障融入业务发展,为全球客户构建可信赖的数字支付生态。围绕全球支付与 AI 智能体商业两大核心应用场景,我们致力于提供全天候、高效率、低成本的跨境支付与结算服务,同时支持AI智能体自主交易、实时结算及高频微支付,加速数字价值在全球范围内的高效流通,拓展智能经济时代的商业新机遇。连接全球支付,赋能AI经济。

Reap (https://reap.global): Reap 是一家全球金融科技公司,透過穩定幣原生基礎設施,協助世界各地的企業連接金融網絡及獲取金融服務。我們融合傳統金融與數碼資產,提升資金流動效率,連繫不同經濟體與主要金融市場,推動金融格局轉型。

Reap 是全球率先將穩定幣融入旗下解決方案的企業之一,處理以穩定幣注資的交易資金流,規模達數十億美元。從支援穩定幣的企業卡到跨境支付,我們透過整合式企業帳戶及嵌入式金融解決方案,簡化企業的財務營運,助力業務拓展。2026 年,Reap 獲 Kraken 母公司 Payward 以 6 億美元收購,成為亞洲金融科技領域最大規模的企業退出交易之一。

Reap 於香港成立,總部亦設於香港,全球員工人數達 300 人。

Utila (https://utila.io/): Utila 是為銀行、金融科技公司、支付服務供應商及企業打造的穩定幣與數碼資產基礎設施平台。機構可透過 Utila,在自主掌控的基礎設施上建立、管理及擴展穩定幣支付、資金管理、交易及代幣化業務。Utila 已獲超過 400 家企業信賴,每月處理的交易額超過 300 億美元,至今累計促成的交易額已突破 5,000 億美元。

讓一切,自由流動

因為價值流動不息,推動價值的人亦然。藉著2026年香港金融科技週的東風,我們將高淨值人士、專業投資者、機構代表、傳統金融資深人士與 Web3 建設者匯聚一堂 - - 讓資本、創意與人脈,如杯中物般自由流動。

不設論壇,不設路演。只有源源供應的免費酒水茶點,以及金融科技週期間最值得一聽的深度對話 - - 就在中環核心。無論您正在促成交易、尋覓下一個機會,還是純粹想身處行業目光所在之處,這一夜,值得您清空日程。

攜想法而來,攜機遇而歸 - - 或許下一個行業藍圖,就誕生於今晚的舉杯之間。

本活動由 EX.

IO 與 Alpha Ladder 聯合主辦,特別感謝贊助商 SPD 及 Reap 的支持 - - 從整合式跨境金融服務、貿易融資與資產代幣化,到穩定幣驅動的全球支付基礎設施,我們秉持同一信念:讓價值自由流動。

盛裝赴會,暢所欲言。讓價值,流動不息。

## From Yield Bearing Stablecoins, Digital Asset Custodians to Layer 1 protocols: Opportunities at the Intersection of Web3 & TradFi

- Record: `luma-crypto-DqOeGl4izFiC1WT`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

### About the event

Join Nara, Hex Trust and XDC Network during Hong Kong FinTech Week to explore opportunities at the intersection of Web3 and traditional finance, covering yield-bearing stablecoins, digital asset custody and Layer 1 protocols.

Connect with industry leaders for an insightful panel discussion and networking

:

- | 4 November 2026 | HKT
- 10:00-10:30 AM: Registration & Networking
- 10:30-11:15 AM: Panel Discussion with 3 panelists and a moderator
- 11:15 AM-12:00 PM: Networking

### About Nara

Nara is a PayFi protocol offering a yield-bearing synthetic dollar backed by short-term financing against payment and receivables flows. Stablecoin payments are moving faster than the liquidity infrastructure around them. Stablecoins can settle near-instantly, but many payment companies still need to bridge delays between fiat collection, on/off-ramp conversion, local payout settlement, and stablecoin funding. That timing gap creates working-capital demand. Nara is the liquidity layer for the stablecoin economy because our goal is not simply to produce yield; our goal is to finance useful payment activity with transparent risk allocation.

### About Hex Trust

Hex Trust is a fully-licensed and regulated financial institution for digital assets. It offers a full suite of Markets services, OTC trading, Custody, Staking and Investment Solutions to builders, investors, and service providers. Hex Trust have a global presence with offices in Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai.

The mission is to unlock ownership in decentralized markets, with a vision to secure the permissionless future.

### About XDC Network

XDC Network is an enterprise-grade Layer 1 blockchain designed to support trade finance, payments, and the tokenization of real-world assets. Its EVM-compatible infrastructure provides fast settlement, low transaction costs, and energy-efficient performance, enabling institutions, businesses, and developers to build scalable blockchain solutions. Learn more at xinfin.org (https://xinfin.org).

We look forward to welcoming you for a morning of insightful discussions, meaningful connections and new opportunities at the intersection of Web3 and traditional finance.

## RWA 2.0:从资产上链到金融机会触达

- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

### About the event

一、活動背景

Openvault 將於 2026 年 11 月 4 日 聯合 Techub News 在香港灣仔舉辦主題活動 「RWA 2.0:從資產上鏈到金融機會觸達」。

香港金融科技周 x StartmeupHK 是亞洲規模最大、影響力最廣的金融科技旗艦盛會。2026 年,兩大盛事進一步合流,以「Fintech Nexus:Bridging the World, Building the Future」為主題,圍繞 AI+、Finance+、Go Global 三大引擎展開,匯聚來自全球 120+ 經濟體的 45,000+ 行業領袖、1,000+ 演講嘉賓、800+ 贊助商/參展商/初創企業,以及 30+ 內地與國際貿易代表團。主論壇於 11 月 2-3 日在香港會議展覽中心舉行,隨後一週延伸至全港多個場地及粵港澳大灣區,舉辦數百場社區與周邊活動。

在金融科技週數百場周邊活動之中,「RWA 2.0」聚焦其中最接近落地的一段賽道:資產完成上鏈之後,金融機會如何真正觸達市場。

───────────────────────────

二、主題闡釋:為什麼是 RWA 2.0

過去兩年,RWA 完成了從概念驗證到批量發行的第一步。政府數字債券、代幣化基金、私募信貸等項目相繼落地,香港的監管框架與沙盒機制亦逐步成型。

資產上鏈解決的是「發行」問題。 債券、基金、私募信貸、商業地產等傳統資產透過代幣化進入鏈上世界,獲得了可分割、可編程、可跨境流轉的新形態。

但發行不等於流動性,上鏈不等於被配置。 分銷渠道能否打通持牌體系?專業投資者如何在合規框架下完成認購與轉讓?二級市場的深度從何而來?這些「最後一公里」的問題,決定 RWA 是停留在技術敘事,還是成為真實的資產類別。

這正是 RWA 2.0 的命題:從「能發行」走向「有人買」。 活動將匯聚資產發行方、資產管理機構、持牌交易平台與合規專業人士,圍繞分銷機制、流動性建設與投資者觸達路徑,分享一線實踐與監管觀察。

三、活動信息

- 日期與時間:2026 年 11 月 4 日(星期三)14:00. 18:00
- 地點:香港灣仔
- 主辦:Openvault | 聯合主辦:Techub News

### About the event

Global Access for Institutional Network. GAIN Edition 5 by Liminal Custody is pleased to invite you to an invite-only banking forum, held in partnership with the Middle East Stablecoin Association (MESA). It brings together banks, regulators, and advisers who are building digital asset capabilities today.

Banks know why they need these capabilities. The harder step is moving from mandate to live implementation. This session focuses on practitioners who have made that move. No vendor pitches. Just what works and what doesn't.

This curated gathering is designed for senior decision-makers seeking:

- Clarity on where banks see the strongest commercial opportunities across custody, stablecoins and cross-border payments, and tokenisation.
- Insight into build-vs-buy, governance, technology, risk and compliance approvals, and operational readiness.
- Direct dialogue with regulators, advisers, and bank practitioners shaping the region's market.

### About the event

Workshop led by Osman Siddiqui

Payments don't break at the ledger. They break in the last mile, where money meets a real user, a real bank, a real edge case.

We'll dig into what actually happens after the transaction clears: off-ramps, settlement delays, compliance friction, and the failure modes that only show up at scale. Expect real examples of where teams got the last mile wrong, and what fixed it.

Walk out with a checklist for the last mile of your own payment flow, before your users find the gaps for you.

- Record: `luma-crypto-vU811G7xGdKFIos`

### About the event

Workshop led by Peter The Speaker

Your customers aren't choosing your competitor because of a feature gap. They're choosing them for reasons you haven't bothered to ask about.

We'll dig into what actually drives customer decisions beneath the stated reasons: the jobs they're hiring your product to do, the switching costs they're weighing, and the unspoken trade-offs that keep them loyal to someone else. You'll map your own customer base against this framework live, testing your assumptions against what's really going on.

Walk out with a clear-eyed read on why you're losing deals you thought you'd win, and a plan to close the gap.

### About Build for Breakpoint

You have until Nov 18 to apply for accelerators that have $125m in funding available. The key to success is showing PMF, and Build for Breakpoint gives you the plan, mentors, and community to win.

Superteam is a global co-operative organised into regional non-profit organisations across 20+ countries focused on supporting founders and talent building at the frontier of tech.

### Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026 | Exclusive Industry Salon

Shaping the Next Chapter of Global Finance

The global financial landscape is undergoing a profound transformation. As digital assets become increasingly integrated into institutional markets, investment, trading, and financial infrastructure are entering a new era of innovation.

At the forefront of this evolution, Hong Kong continues to strengthen its position as a global financial hub. As of May 2026, 13 virtual asset trading platforms had been licensed by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC). Meanwhile, Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026 is expected to convene over 45,000 industry leaders from more than 120 economies, underscoring the city's growing influence in global financial innovation.

As traditional finance and digital assets converge, the industry is moving beyond market exploration toward institutional adoption and real-world implementation.

Against this backdrop, Interlace and QingShi Securities will co-host an exclusive, invitation-only industry salon during Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026. Bringing together 50-60 senior financial executives, institutional investors, and industry leaders, the event will explore emerging opportunities at the intersection of traditional finance, digital assets, and fintech

Key Discussion Themes

Brokerage × Digital Assets | Unlocking new opportunities in institutional financial services

On-Chain Assets | Asset tokenization and the future of investment infrastructure

Fintech × Financial Services | Building the next generation of financial infrastructure

Institutional Adoption & Execution | Turning market opportunities into real-world business application

### Event Details

Date: November 6, 2026 | Hong Kong FinTech Week

Time: 14:00-18:00 HKT

Location: Hong Kong | Venue details shared upon confirmation Format: Invitation-Only Executive Salon

Attendance: 50-60 Selected Guests

Limited availability. All registrations are subject to approval.

Welcome to join our Wechat Group

### About Interlace

https://www.interlace.money/

Interlace is building stablecoin banking infrastructure that connects on-chain assets with real-world financial rails. We help businesses use stablecoins as seamlessly as fiat for cross-border payments, card issuing, global accounts, treasury management, and payment acquiring. (8M+ cards issued, trusted by 20,000+ businesses).

https://www.interlace.money/

Interlace 致力于构建稳定币银行基础设施，连接链上资产与现实世界的金融体系，让企业能够像使用法币一样便捷地使用稳定币。通过跨境支付、全球发卡、全球账户、资金管理及支付收单等一站式金融服务，Interlace 助力企业实现高效、便捷的全球资金流转。目前，Interlace 已累计发行 800万+ 张支付卡，获得全球 20,000+ 家企业客户的信赖。

### About Azure Lion Securities

https://algroup.com.hk/#/home

Azure Lion Securities is a technology-driven financial services platform based in Hong Kong, offering securities trading, investment advisory, asset management and family office services. Combining digital trading capabilities with personalised wealth management, we connect entrepreneurs, professional investors and families with global capital markets

Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026｜高端金融行业闭门沙龙

共话全球金融创新的下一篇章

全球金融体系正迎来新一轮结构性变革。随着数字资产加速融入机构金融市场，投资、交易及金融基础设施正在经历深刻演进。

随着传统金融与数字资产加速融合，行业关注点正从市场探索走向机构参与与实际业务落地。

## London Workshop: Vaults in Practice – How Financial Institutions Capture Onchain Yield

- Record: `luma-crypto-futrlVtSKm5AC1e`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-09T16:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/cwufkzk1>

### About the event

This workshop provides a structured, case-study-driven deep dive into onchain vaults as the key primitive of DeFi and tokenized capital markets, led by Steakhouse Financial.

Starting from familiar concepts such as funds and ETFs, the session explains how vaults represent the next step in the evolution of asset management. combining programmable execution, non-custodial design, and real-time risk management. Participants will gain a practical understanding of how vaults work, how they differ from traditional investment vehicles, and why they are increasingly adopted by institutions.

The discussion then moves from fundamentals into live production environments, examining how vaults are deployed, operated, and integrated today. This includes institutional use cases such as platform integrations, as well as operational and compliance considerations when running vault strategies in regulated contexts.

From there, the workshop explores where vault management is expanding next, using concrete production case studies curated and operated by Steakhouse Financial:

RWA as collateral (Fasanara mF-ONE)

Fixed-term lending and yield structuring via Pendle

- Leveraged vault strategies (Steakhouse High Yield Turbo)

By the end of the session, attendees will have a clear, example-driven understanding of how vaults are used in practice today, and how the frontier of vault management is shaping the next generation of institutional onchain products.

About Steakhouse Financial Steakhouse Financial is the leading curator on DeFi Money Markets (Morpho, Kamino), building earn products for the future of the stablecoin economy. Steakhouse Financial operates at the intersection of real world assets, protocol design, and data-driven DeFi portfolio management. They aspire to empower the world with institutional-grade DeFi tools to raise, manage and distribute the capital they need to make a difference.

For questions, please contact: mail@blockstories.io

### About the event

Who carries the regulatory risk when money moves onchain? How are sanctions reshaping the digital assets landscape?

The night before Digital Assets Summit London, Range and Fieldfisher are hosting an evening for those shaping how digital assets are transforming financial services.

We're bringing together senior finance, treasury, compliance, risk and legal leaders working across stablecoins, digital assets and fiat for an exclusive event.

Galiya Martirosova, a member of Fieldfisher's Sanctions Group, and Farheen Ishtiaq-Stansfeld, from Fieldfisher's Commercial Crime team, join Range for a fireside discussion on sanctions and financial crime risk as institutions start moving value on stablecoin rails, and the governance questions that come with it.

After questions from the room, an evening drinks reception will follow. The conversation will respect the Chatham House Rule and will not be recorded. No slides, no pitches, no panels.

Please bring photo ID. Fieldfisher's visitor procedure requires it for entry, and guests without it cannot be admitted.

Spots are limited. Register now

### About Fieldfisher

Fieldfisher is an enterprising European law firm built around people. It has market-leading practices in four key sectors of energy and natural resources, technology, financial services and life sciences. Fieldfisher helps clients keep pace with an unpredictable and continually evolving world, with a sector-diverse team of specialist dispute resolution lawyers on hand to assist with conflicts, whatever the size or subject matter. The firm's network spans over 2,200 people across 28 international offices in 14 countries, all of which offer clients highly commercial, pragmatic advice.

Fieldfisher advises businesses across the digital assets ecosystem on navigating an evolving regulatory landscape, managing risk and disputes, and capitalising on new opportunities in financial technology.

For more information: https://www.fieldfisher.com

### About Range

Range is the leading stablecoin treasury and risk management platform for financial institutions, trusted by the Solana Foundation, Circle, Stellar, Squads, and more. We provide the compliance, risk, and routing systems required to manage and move digital assets safely across blockchains.

Used by fintechs, asset issuers, and custodians, our platform acts as the system of record for digital asset treasuries, aggregating balances, transactions, and counterparties across wallets, custodians, exchanges, and blockchains.

Whether you're building programmable treasuries or privacy flows, Range helps ensure they're safe, compliant, and ready for scale.

Learn more at range.org (https://range.org).

The address is only shown to approved guests.

Moving money across Africa is still slow, expensive and fragmented. FX friction, multi-day settlement and layered intermediary fees hold back trade, remittances and treasury operations across the continent. The real cost of cross-border payments and FX across African corridors

## Bitcoin on Sui: Getting Started with Hashi

- Record: `luma-crypto-M0D3pED64DdvZ74`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-12T11:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/ticfmzzo>

### About the event

Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle capital in crypto, and most of it never moves, because using it anywhere else has meant handing it to a custodian or a wrapped-token bridge. Hashi is Sui's answer. Your BTC stays on Bitcoin, held at an address controlled jointly by Hashi's validator committee, which signs with threshold MPC, and an independent guardian layer. Against it, hBTC is minted on Sui and works across Sui apps. Burn the hBTC and the BTC is released back on Bitcoin. Hashi is now live on Sui mainnet in a phased rollout, partners first, backed by more than $500 million in commitments from over 20 partners including Anchorage Digital. In early November about 9.

6 hBTC had been minted onchain, and you can watch that number grow. This session explains how Hashi works under the hood and gets you building with it. We read the live mainnet deployment directly: the Hashi object, the deposit and withdrawal queues, the committee and the hBTC supply. Then we use the Hashi TypeScript SDK on testnet with Bitcoin signet to run the full user journey: generate a personal Bitcoin deposit address for a Sui account, send signet BTC to it, follow the deposit through committee approval until hBTC is minted, and request a withdrawal back to Bitcoin. You build hBTC Desk, a small app that runs the testnet round trip and shows the live mainnet numbers beside it.

What You'll Learn - How Hashi keeps BTC on Bitcoin: per-account deposit addresses, joint control by the validator committee and the guardian layer, threshold MPC signing, and how hBTC is minted and burned - What is live today: reading the mainnet package, the deposit and withdrawal queues and the hBTC supply with GraphQL, and what a phased rollout means for builders - The SDK: @mysten/hashi, generating a deposit address, submitting a deposit, tracking its status, and requesting or cancelling a withdrawal - Building on hBTC: using it like any other Sui coin in your own Move code and programmable transactions, with 8 decimals and integer base units from end to end - Honest limits: the SDK is pre-1. 0 and not yet wired to mainnet, deposits wait for Bitcoin confirmations and a time delay, and how to show pending states so nobody pays twice - How to ship hBTC Desk: deposit signet BTC, watch hBTC arrive on Sui testnet, withdraw back to a Bitcoin address, and compare it with the live mainnet numbers

Who Should Attend - DeFi builders who want Bitcoin as collateral in lending, trading or vaults - Wallet and payments teams that want to hold and move BTC inside Sui apps - Developers who joined the bridging and CCTP sessions and want the Bitcoin side of the story - Bitcoin holders curious how BTC can be used on another chain without giving up custody to a single company What to Bring - Laptop with Node.js 22+ and pnpm, and the latest @mysten/sui and @mysten/hashi - A Sui testnet wallet - A Bitcoin wallet that supports signet, such as Sparrow. We share a signet faucet in class - Basic TypeScript.

No Bitcoin scripting required Join us at SuiHub to learn, build, and connect with fellow developers pushing the boundaries of the Sui ecosystem.

<a id="event-9c53c7dcc26fad9c"></a>

## Race Against the Machine: AI, Quantum and the Future of Bitcoin

- Record: `luma-crypto-MEbXp19ZPmMKn0A`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-12T16:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/j8ks5br9>

### Intro

Almost everything we trust online, from banking and web traffic to messaging and digital identity, rests on public-key cryptography. Two threats are now calling that very foundation into question. Quantum computers could break today's signatures and key exchange, with the hardware required shrinking steadily. AI could reach the same result with breakthroughs in mathematics, and it is already helping quantum attacks along by optimizing the circuits behind them.

The synergy between them is unmistakable, and even the post-quantum schemes meant to replace today's cryptography may not be safe either. With finance and the internet facing a long, fragmented migration, the stakes are highest where cryptography protects value directly. Cryptocurrencies add their own exposure: public keys sit on a public ledger, assets are bearer instruments, and theft is irreversible. Given Bitcoin's history, the challenge is particularly acute: every serious option (do nothing, freeze, force a deadline) violates a principle the Bitcoin community cares about, and the work must start before the threat is visible.

Join us at this interdisciplinary event where AI, quantum and Bitcoin experts come together in a novel panel to discuss the technical foundations of this challenge and its potential solutions

### Program

17:00 Arrival 17:30 Intro 17:35 Keynote 1: Quantum 17:55 Keynote 2: Bitcoin 18:15 Q&A 19:00 Networkin

### Speakers

Wadim Wormsbecher:

> Theoretical physicist turned tech innovator. With a PhD from Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and a background developing AI products, Wadim now works at Bundesdruckerei focusing on applied cybersecurity in the era of Quantum and AI. His focus goes beyond hardware. AI-driven discoveries and algorithmic improvements can reduce the resources needed to challenge today's cryptography. Understanding these shifts is essential to assessing quantum threats and making informed security decisions. > > https://www.linkedin.com/in/wadimwormsbecher/

Fabian Jahr:

> Fabian Jahr has contributed to Bitcoin Core since 2019 and currently works on it full-time with a grant from Brink. He reviews critical changes to Bitcoin Core, develops ASMap for a more decentralized peer-to-peer network, and researches protocol upgrades. With the support of the Human Rights Foundation, he published a report on how Cross-Input Signature Aggregation could change Bitcoin, and he is now turning it into a soft fork proposal with BIPs 458 to 460. > > https://fjahr.com/ https://brink.dev/

Manuel Moran:

> Over the past 12 years, Manuel has built software across research, media, and both traditional and decentralized finance. His path has run from software engineering, through data science and machine learning, to AI engineering, where he now owns end-to-end agentic workflows. At the ephesto consultancy he collaborates with experts in design, strategy, finance, and law to help organizations stay competitive as AI redefines what it takes to be successful. > > https://ephesto.com/

This event is organized by Leap Quantum Technology Hub as part of the Thursday Gathering by Venture Café Berlin.

https://leap.berlin/ https://venturecafeberlin.org/

## Whitepaper Reading SF - Defi Topics: No Place to Hide & Active Liquidity On Chain

- Record: `luma-crypto-bDcxH60c9qvNp0x`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-11-13T01:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/snrgc7jo>

### About the event

Discussion Topics As more trading moves through private RPCs and protected submission channels, the question is how much safety those protections actually buy. No Place to Hide examines three years of activity across six chains and finds sandwich attacks against supposedly protected transactions on four of them. The exposure comes from order-flow auctions, validators, applications, reorgs, and even an RPC bug. We'll ask what "protected" should mean when keeping a trade out of the public mempool still leaves multiple ways for attackers to see it coming, and whether protection can hold without securing the full path from wallet to execution.

We'll also cover Active Liquidity On Chain, a study of proprietary AMMs across Solana, Base, and Monad. These venues let a single operator supply inventory and update prices without waiting for a trade, helping them avoid the stale quotes that arbitrageurs exploit in passive AMMs. The paper finds better prices for flow used as a proxy for retail trading, alongside pricing that varies by counterparty and evidence of quotes that worsen at execution. The core discussion is whether tighter spreads justify opaque pricing rules, and how aggregators should route trades when the price they see may differ from the price users receive.  Reading Overview

No Place to Hide: Where private transaction protections fail, and what it takes to secure the full path from wallet to execution.

Active Liquidity On Chain: How proprietary AMMs improve pricing, and the trade-offs around transparency, routing, and execution quality. Full Documents

No Place to Hide (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28115)

Active Liquidity On Chain (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38056) Format

- 10 minutes of silent reading to start.

Discussion first, with no panels.

Bring questions - technical depth is welcomed.

Short notes and key takeaways shared after the session. About Whitepaper Reading Club Whitepaper Reading Club is a community of 800 builders, founders, and researchers across Singapore, Malaysia, San Francisco, Lagos, Bangkok, and New York. The community meets in person every month to discuss the latest blockchain projects. The club creates detailed, easy-to-understand summaries for each paper and has held more than 70 sessions since June 2023, covering topics from Account Abstraction, Parallel Chains, and EIPs to the Bitcoin ecosystem and AI × crypto. It is ecosystem-agnostic and not for profit, with a strong focus on projects with technical, product, or social innovations.

Dimes, our community partner, connects builders with the people, resources, and support to turn ideas into reality. Our host venue, localhost, is Dimes' co-working and event space in downtown San Francisco, created for builders to meet, share ideas, and connect. We're excited to host this event with Whitepaper Reading Club.  #Crypto

About This Event TSC Summit East Coast brings the Trusted Smart Chain community together in Fort Lauderdale for a weekend of connection, education, and an inside look at what's ahead. Node owners, founding community members, and prospective members are invited to join us for two days centered around Trusted Smart Chain, including where the ecosystem stands today, the continued development of Nova DAO governance, and the future of native RWA+ issuance on TSC. The weekend begins

Friday evening with a waterfront Welcome Dinner hosted by T7X. On Saturday, attendees will hear directly from members of the Founding Team during a full day of TSC overview sessions, updates, and discussions, beginning with morning coffee and continuing through the afternoon with lunch provided. One

registration includes access to both Friday and Saturday events. There is a separate

registration for the VIP Titan + event. Room Block Discounted accommodations are available based on first come first serve through our official event room block: visit the official page to > Reserve Your Room (https://book.passkey.com/event/51348812/owner/4894/home?utm_campaign=301742827)

What This Summit Is About Capital Markets, Rebuilt Trusted Smart Chain is a Layer 1 blockchain engineered to support the tokenization of Real-World Assets (RWA+), creating infrastructure designed to serve institutions and individuals alike. Community Governance Nova DAO brings decentralized governance to the TSC ecosystem, giving participating node owners and community members a voice in the continued development and direction of the network.

- 12:00 PM Lunch Caribbean IV-V

Ledger: Ledger's main activity is the security of digital assets. It designs and markets hardware and software for managing and securing crypto assets. Olympix: Olympix is an pre-audit smart contract testing platform that secures more than $155B in assets across customers such as Circle, Aave, Securitize, and Ethena. It allows teams to surface audit level findings and what audits and AI miss during development. The venue Juno, Olympia: Juno is the UK's biggest Italian restaurant, run by Incipio Group in the Grade II listed National Hall at Olympia. ## La Casa de Satoshi cumple 2 años 🎉 \| Lanzamiento oficial del Libro BitcoinCoach

- Record: `luma-crypto-zofPb94imH95qhz`

### About the event

¡La Casa de Satoshi cumple dos años! ¿Quieres pagar con Bitcoin? Encontrarás las instrucciones al final de esta página. Para celebrarlo, estamos preparando el evento más grande que hemos organizado hasta ahora: un domingo completo dedicado a la comunidad Bitcoin de México, a las personas que la hacen posible y a los proyectos que están construyendo su futuro. Para esta celebración nos hemos aliado con Rodrigo Coutiño, reconocido autor de libros best seller como MoneyCoach, InvestorCoach y BusinessCoach, para presentar el lanzamiento oficial de su nueva obra: BitcoinCoach.

El domingo 15 de noviembre de 2026 reuniremos en La Casa de Satoshi a emprendedores, comunidades, empresas, educadores y bitcoiners de todo el país. Será una celebración de todo lo que hemos construido juntos durante estos dos años y, al mismo tiempo, el comienzo de una nueva etapa para La Casa de Satoshi.

Durante el evento tendremos: El lanzamiento oficial de BitcoinCoach, presentado por su autor, Rodrigo Coutiño. Después de la presentación, Rodrigo convivirá con la comunidad y firmará ejemplares del libro. Lightning pitches de proyectos y empresas Bitcoin en México. Hasta diez participantes tendrán entre dos y tres minutos para compartir lo que están construyendo. La historia de La Casa de Satoshi y un anuncio especial sobre su futuro, presentado por Santiago Varela Belmont junto con el equipo de la Casa. ₿ Un anuncio especial de Aureo, presentado por Gustavo Flores Echaiz, seguido del arranque oficial de la fiesta. Una gran parrillada para celebrar el aniversario.

Música, convivencia y muchas oportunidades para conocer a las personas que están impulsando Bitcoin en México.

¿Qué incluye tu boleto? Un ejemplar de BitcoinCoach de Rodrigo Coutiño, con un precio habitual de $389 MXN en Amazon. Conoce el libro aquí (https://investor.com.mx/bitcoincoach/). Acceso a todas las presentaciones y actividades del programa. Parrillada y bebidas. Si ya has venido a alguna de nuestras fiestas, sabes que se pone bueno. ¡La fiesta de aniversario de La Casa de Satoshi! Maciej Cepnik será el maestro de ceremonias. Este encuentro es para toda la comunidad: quienes han estado con nosotros desde el comienzo, quienes se han sumado durante estos dos años y quienes visitarán La Casa de Satoshi por primera vez.

Queremos reunir en un mismo lugar a la comunidad Bitcoin más grande de México para celebrar lo que ya existe, descubrir nuevos proyectos y compartir todo lo que viene. Las empresas, startups y proyectos participantes se anunciarán próximamente.

Programa preliminar 12:00 p. m. | Apertura de puertas y recepción Registro, convivencia y recepción de asistentes. ¡Llega temprano! Tendremos sorpresas, libros y mucho más para quienes nos acompañen desde el inicio. 1:00-1:30 p. m. | Lanzamiento oficial de BitcoinCoach Presentación del nuevo libro con su autor, Rodrigo Coutiño. 1:30-2:00 p. m. | Lightning pitches Hasta diez presentaciones de proyectos, empresas y comunidades que trabajan con Bitcoin en México. Cada participante tendrá entre dos y tres minutos, con breves intervenciones entre las presentaciones.

2:00-2:15 p. m. | La historia y el futuro de La Casa de Satoshi Celebración de los dos años, presentación del equipo y anuncio especial de Santiago Varela Belmont sobre la nueva etapa de La Casa de Satoshi. 2:15-2:30 p. m. | Anuncio especial de Aureo y arranque de la fiesta Presentación de Gustavo Flores Echaiz y apertura oficial de la celebración. A partir de las 2:30 p. m. | Parrillada y fiesta de aniversario Firma de libros y fotografías con Rodrigo Coutiño, música, comida, convivencia y networking con la comunidad. 7:00 p. m. | Cierre del evento Los horarios son aproximados y podrán ajustarse conforme confirmemos a los proyectos, empresas e invitados participantes.

La Casa de Satoshi, Ciudad de México Domingo 15 de noviembre de 2026 Puertas abiertas desde las 12:00 p. m. Inicio del programa a la 1:00 p. m. Ven a celebrar con nosotros dos años de encuentros, aprendizaje, amistad y construcción comunitaria. ¡Nos vemos en la gran fiesta de aniversario de La Casa de Satoshi!  ₿

¿Quieres pagar con Bitcoin? Haz clic en el botón de boletos con Bitcoin y completa tu registro. Después recibirás un correo de maciej@aureobitcoin.com con las instrucciones para realizar tu pago con Bitcoin. Si quieres aprovechar el descuento por pagar con Bitcoin, pero todavía no tienes, visita aureobitcoin.com (https://aureobitcoin.com) para comprar tus primeros bitcoins.

Patrocinado por Aureo Este evento es patrocinado por Aureobitcoin.com (https://www.aureobitcoin.com/es), la plataforma Bitcoin de México para personas, empresas y patrimonios. Aureo facilita la compra y venta de Bitcoin con precios transparentes y custodia bajo el control de cada usuario. También ofrece soluciones especializadas para tesorerías empresariales, operaciones OTC y gestión patrimonial, acompañadas de atención personalizada e investigación enfocada en el mercado mexicano.

You're invited to a private dinner hosted by Privy & Bridge. Join a select group of leaders across fintech, payments and web3 for an intimate evening of great food and thoughtful conversation. This includes Privy's embedded wallet infrastructure and Bridge's stablecoin orchestration capabilities, enabling businesses to hold, move, and spend money across traditional and blockchain rails.

Visa (https://www.visa.co.uk/) is a global leader in digital payments, connecting consumers, businesses and financial institutions across more than 200 countries and territories. Open Standard (https://joinopenstandard.com/)is the company behind Open USD (OUSD). Over 200 financial institutions, fintechs, banks, and global businesses have signed up to add OUSD to their platforms and benefit from low fees, shared rewards, and representative governance. Open Standard was started in 2026 and its founding partners include Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa.

### About the event

In 1698, London's stockbrokers were thrown out of the Royal Exchange for bad manners. They moved into a coffee house down the alley, and that's where the London Stock Exchange began. In 1986, Big Bang put the trading floor on screens. Forty years on in 2026, it's happening again. Stocks, treasuries, perps, prediction markets, memecoins and AI traders are all heading on-chain at once, the inflection point is here. So we've done the sensible thing and taken over a pub. Creating a stronghold of the best in the biz for complimentary refreshments all day.

On Monday 16 November, day two of Solana Breakpoint, the Zebu Live Arms opens at the Bush Tavern in Shepherd's Bush, a short walk from Olympia. One day with the people moving markets: traders, market makers, exchanges, funds, founders.

TRADING HOURS 11:00 | Doors: Tea, Coffee, Bacon butties and a table for your meetings 12:00 | Opening Bell & debates 13:00 | Lunch: burgers, loaded fries, the works 14:30 | The Exchange: pub debates & creator sessions 17:00 | After Hours: espresso martinis and spicy margs, followed up with open bar + chatting shop 21:00 | Closing Bell: Last orders Speakers announced shortly Food and drink on us all day, please note this event is Invite only: request to join and we'll confirm your spot. Meet your hosts: Zebu Live is the UK's flagship Web3 summit, bringing the community together for over 5 years of industry-defining conversations that drive the space forward. Disrupt today. Discover tomorrow.

AlphaWire is a crypto news and analysis platform built for people who trade, build and invest in crypto. Its focus is the story behind the headline, with insight straight from the builders, before the narrative breaks. Its free daily briefing, Alpha Club, is read by 47,000+ builders, operators and investors. Visit their page: https://alphawire.xyz/ Our partners MetaMask The world's open money app, with over 100 million downloads. Swap, trade perps, tokenised stocks and prediction markets, earn on your stablecoins and spend with a card, across Solana, Ethereum, Bitcoin and dozens more chains, all from one app. Wincent Algorithms meet digital asset markets.

A top 10 global market maker trading since 2017, with $5B+ traded daily across 300+ digital assets and 15+ exchanges. Stand With Crypto UK A grassroots movement of more than 311,000 advocates across the UK, bringing users, founders and builders together to help make the UK the best place to build, grow and use digital assets. HT Digital Specialist accountants and auditors for the digital asset industry, advising crypto businesses since 2017 on audit, tax, accounting and proof of reserves. Superteam UK The home for web3 and frontier tech in the UK, backed by the Solana Foundation. They've supported 200+ startups and helped founders raise $40M+, with co-working hubs from London to Glasgow.

Community partners MonkeDAO Premier Web3.0 Country Club, a global community built around the Solana Monkey Business (SMB) collection on Solana.
